attribution: Wimmer W, Anschuetz L, Weder S, Wagner F, Delingette H, Caversaccio M (2019). Human Bony Labyrinth: Co-Registered CT and micro-CT Images, Surface Models and Anatomical Landmarks. Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.3355272. CC BY 4.0.
modifications: Micro-CT surface of specimen F07 (right) labelled into cochlea, vestibule and semicircular canals in the specimen cochlear frame, simplified by 0.24 mm vertex clustering, and placed by a similarity transform (oval window to the Z-Anatomy stapes footplate, part centroids to the former Z-Anatomy inner-ear positions, refined by whole-shape ICP). Left side is a reflected display copy.

coordinates.sourceToApp: Source millimetres, scale 1.0451, rotation and translation in source-provenance.json.

limitations: One adult right specimen; the left ear is its mirror image, not an independent specimen.
Bony labyrinth (otic capsule lumen) only; membranous labyrinth, cochlear duct and nerve endings are not modelled.
Part boundaries are geometric cuts in the cochlear frame, not segmented anatomical borders.
Placement is fitted to the connected body ear; exact position relative to the temporal bone is approximate.
